title: Cloud Computing and Its Applications
content: The Department of Interdisciplinary Courses in Engineering (DICE), Chitkara University, organized a webinar on “Cloud Computing and Its Applications” on 28 March 2026. The session was delivered by Shashank Tripathi, Technical Trainer at PyNet Labs, Gurugram, Haryana. The webinar witnessed enthusiastic participation from students and faculty members across various disciplines. During the session, the expert provided a comprehensive overview of cloud computing, highlighting its importance in modern computing environments. He explained why cloud computing is widely adopted, emphasizing benefits such as cost efficiency, scalability, flexibility, reliability, and on-demand self-service. The session covered cloud computing services delivered over the internet, supported by real-world examples to help participants understand its relevance in daily life. The expert elaborated on various cloud service models, including Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS), Platform as a Service (PaaS), and Software as a Service (SaaS), along with development models. Further, different cloud deployment models were discussed, including public cloud, private cloud, hybrid cloud, and community cloud, explaining their features and use cases. The speaker also provided insights into career opportunities in cloud computing, discussing various job roles such as Cloud Engineer, Cloud Developer, SysOps Administrator, Cloud Architect, DevOps Engineer, Cloud Security Engineer, and Data Engineer, along with their average salary ranges in India. Additionally, the session included guidance on industry-recognized certifications such as AWS Certification. The expert also shared useful learning resources and platforms related to Amazon Web Services and Microsoft Azure, enabling participants to explore hands-on practice and further skill development in cloud technologies. He also demonstrated how to host a web service using a Linux operating system and deploy a website on the cloud, providing practical exposure to real-world implementation. An interactive question-and-answer session was conducted, where participants actively engaged with the speaker, raising queries related to cloud concepts, tools, and career opportunities. The event was aligned with SDG 4 (Quality Education), SDG 5 (Gender Equality), SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure), and SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals), promoting knowledge sharing, inclusivity, innovation, and collaborative learning among participants.

title: AI Driven Research Tools and Safety for Manuscript Writing
content: The Department of Interdisciplinary Courses in Engineering (DICE), Chitkara University, organized a webinar on “AI Driven Research Tools and Safety for Manuscript Writing” on 21 March 2026. The session was delivered by Dr. Brijesh Mishra, Associate Professor, CMR University, Bengaluru. The webinar witnessed active participation from more than 125 participants from across India, including students, researchers, and faculty members. During the session, the expert provided valuable insights into a wide range of research and writing tools, including Mendeley, OriginLab, LaTeX, Graph Data Extraction tools, Reuse Permission protocols, MATLAB, ChatGPT, Stealth Writer, Virtual Labs, Grammarly, and QuillBot. The session also included practical demonstrations, enabling participants to gain hands-on understanding of these tools. An interactive question-and-answer segment was conducted, during which participants actively engaged with the expert to clarify their queries related to manuscript writing and research practices. The event was aligned with SDG 4 (Quality Education), SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure), and SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals), fostering innovation, collaboration, and experiential learning among students and faculty members.

title: Machina Inversa
content: On 13th February 2026, the Department of Interdisciplinary Courses in Engineering (DICE), in collaboration with ProtoHub Lab (Tinkerers Lab) and CUIET-AE, organized Machina Inversa—a reverse engineering event that quietly redefined what it means to be an engineer. The session invited students to look beyond polished exteriors and into the logic, circuitry, and design thinking hidden within everyday devices such as ceiling fans, induction cooktops, microwave ovens, drill machines, and even the humble optical mouse. The session was formally initiated by Dr. Rajneesh Talwar, Dean – DICE, who addressed the participants and emphasized the importance of reverse engineering. He highlighted how reverse engineering strengthens analytical thinking, problem-solving skills, and innovation by encouraging students to understand the practical implementation of theoretical concepts. Further Dr.Talwar explained what facilities DICE has been providing along with Projects DICE has done with the students. The event carried a deeper message: engineering is not memorizing formulas, but cultivating the courage to question, analyze, and improve the world around us. He emphasized that DICE is more than a department—it is a mindset where disciplines intersect, ideas evolve, and innovation becomes a habit. Machina Inversa reflected this very philosophy. The technical session was further conducted by Dr. Anukriti Sharma, who provided detailed insights into the devices selected for the activity and explained the various components involved in reverse engineering. Through Dr. Anukriti’s insightful explanations, machines were not merely opened—they were understood. And in that understanding, students discovered something far more powerful than mechanisms and circuits: they rediscovered the essence of engineering itself—curiosity with purpose, knowledge with application, and learning that transforms the way we see the world. Students participated enthusiastically and showcased creativity, teamwork, and technical curiosity throughout the activity. The interactive and hands-on approach made the session highly engaging and enriched the students’ practical understanding of engineering systems while covering SDG 4,SDG 9 and SDG 12. The workshop successfully fostered a spirit of innovation, critical thinking, and hands-on learning among students, reinforcing the importance of practical exposure in engineering education.

title: Understanding Arduino for Innovations and IoT Applications
content: The Department of Interdisciplinary Courses in Engineering (DICE), Chitkara University, organized a hands-on workshop on “Understanding Arduino for Innovations and IoT Applications” on 21st February 2026 in the DICE Lab. The workshop aimed to equip budding engineers with practical exposure to embedded systems and IoT technologies. Dr. Rajneesh Talwar, Professor and Dean, DICE, opened the session with fundamentals of computing, embedded systems, and Arduino technology, highlighting diverse boards such as Lilypad, Mega, Nano, and Uno. He emphasized experiential learning, prototyping, debugging, and optimization as essential skills for engineers. In the second half, Dr. Manvinder Sharma, Associate Professor, provided demonstrations on Arduino Uno programming, device interfacing, and simulations using Tinkercad. Students gained hands-on experience through mini-projects including a Traffic Light Control System and Gas Detection System, learning sensor interfacing, LED control, and real-time data processing. The workshop aligned with SDGs 4, 9, 11, and 12, fostering innovation, sustainability, and quality education.

title: Shiksha Mahakumbh Abhiyan 2025
content: Department of Interdisciplinary Courses in Engineering (DICE), played a key role in organising and coordinating at Shiksha Mahakumbh Abhiyan 2025 which was held from 31st October to 2nd November 2025 at the National Institute of Pharmaceutical Education & Research (NIPER), Mohali, Punjab. The event served as a national platform uniting educators, researchers, innovators, and students from across India to deliberate on the evolving landscape of education and its role in building Viksit Bharat @ 2047. Dr Rajneesh Talwar, Professor & Dean, DICE, Chitkara University, and the team of the department actively contributed to two major events i.e Project display and Paper presentation. the Project Display Event, where innovative projects from schools and colleges across India showcased creativity, technology, and social impact.Dr Talwar chaired the technical session on “EdTech and Digital Education,” where 15 research papers were presented, highlighting transformative ideas in AI-enabled learning, digital pedagogy, and technology-driven education.The contribution of the Department of Interdisciplinary Courses in Engineering (DICE), Chitkara University, in the Shiksha Mahakumbh Abhiyan 2025 underscores the university’s commitment to educational innovation, interdisciplinary collaboration, and national educational development.

title: Exploring Hackathons and Projects with DICE
content:
Dr. Rajneesh Talwar led an engaging session titled 'Exploring Hackathons and Projects with DICE' for first-year students of Computer Science Engineering (CSE), Artificial Intelligence (AI), and Future Technology. The session emphasized the power of innovation, highlighting how technology and creativity can come together to drive meaningful societal impact. Dr. Talwar encouraged students to cultivate an innovative mindset early in their academic journey.
Smart India Hackathon (SIH) 2025: Dr. Talwar provided detailed insights into SIH 2025, a national-level platform that enables students to develop innovative solutions to real-world challenges through teamwork.
The hackathon covers various themes, including:
- Smart Automation,Smart Resource Conservation
Smart Education,Disaster Management
Blockchain & Cybersecurity,Renewable / Sustainable Energy
Travel & Tourism,Clean & Green Technology
Robotics and Drones,Transportation & Logistics,Smart Vehicles
Agriculture, FoodTech & Rural Development,MedTech / BioTech / HealthTech
Heritage & Culture,Fitness & Sports
Toys & Games, Space Technology
Dr. Talwar shared tips on analyzing problem statements, aligning solutions with industry and societal needs, and building effective multidisciplinary teams.
The session inspired students to utilize DICE as a hub for innovation and experimentation, preparing them for SIH 2025 and other hackathons, entrepreneurial ventures, and future-ready projects

title: Techinnovate 2.0
content: Department of Interdisciplinary Courses in Engineering (DICE) at Chitkara University organized “TECHINNOVATE 2.0”, a showcase of creativity and innovation in technology. The event featured the top 36 projects selected from over 200+ submissions. The projects were meticulously curated for their innovation, real world applicability and technical finesse.The event was inaugurated with great enthusiasm by Dr. K.K. Mishra,(Pro Vice Chancellor Accreditation and Quality Assurance Cell), Dr. Rakesh Sharma (Registrar), and Dr. Praveen Kumar Khosla (Pro Vice Chancellor, Advanced research). The event also saw the participation of Dr. Rajeev (Controller of Examinations), and Dr. Shushil Narang, Dean AI . Dr. Rajneesh Talwar, Professor and Dean, DICE, warmly welcomed the dignitaries and accompanied them as they interacted with the students.Students demonstrated a wide array of IoT-based innovations across diverse domains such as smart healthcare, home automation, liquid vending systems, wearable technologies, human follower rovers and stair-climbing robots. The event highlighted the ingenuity and technical acumen of young engineers aiming to solve real-world challenges through smart technology.Among the displayed projects, five outstanding innovations were awarded for their excellence in design, implementation and societal impact. TECHINNOVATE 2.0 served not only as a platform to celebrate student innovation but also as a bridge between academic learning and industry relevance.This event fostered an environment of learning, collaboration, and future-focused thinking, encouraging students to build solutions that contribute meaningfully to society and covered  SDG 3 – Good Health and Well-being, SDG 4 – Quality Education, SDG 7 – Affordable and Clean Energy, SDG 9 – Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure, SDG 11 – Sustainable Cities and Communities, SDG 12 – Responsible Consumption and Production and SDG 17 – Partnerships for the Goals

title: Technovision 4.0
content: The Department of Interdisciplinary Courses in Engineering (DICE) at Chitkara University proudly hosted TECHNOVISION 4.0 — a vibrant celebration of innovation, creativity, and real-world problem-solving. From an automated voice-controlled wheelchair to a gesture-based navigation system for the visually impaired, the event spotlighted 34 standout projects handpicked from over 180+ submissions — each a testament to the ingenuity of our budding engineers.

title: Expert Session By Dr.Rajneesh Talwar for Abstract writing
content: A pre-conference workshop session was organised by CRIO, Chitkara on “Topic: Think, Test, Theorize: Interactive Bootcamp on Psychological Research Design”on 14th July 2025.An expert session was organized for psychology students wherein Dr. Rajneesh Talwar, Dean DICE deliberated on the topic. The session aimed to equip students with the essential skills and techniques required to write an effective abstract for international conference. Dr.Talwar began the session by emphasizing the significance of abstracts in academic submissions, particularly in international conferences and journal where the abstract often determines acceptance and sets the stage for presentation impact. Key points covered included: Understanding the Abstract Structure, Characteristics of a Good Abstract, Common Mistakes to Avoid, Tips for Success. The session also included a practical segment where students were shared a sample abstracts based on hypothetical research topics. The session was informative and well-received by the participants. Dr. Rajneesh Talwar’s expertise and engaging delivery greatly enhanced the students’ understanding of abstract writing. The session concluded with an interactive Q&A, allowing students to clarify doubts and gain deeper insight into academic writing standards for international platforms.

title: Vigyaan Manthan 2025
content: Department of Interdisciplinary courses in engineering (DICE) showcased 30 Projects in "Vigyaan Manthan 2025" held at Chitkara University, Punjab in alpha zone on 24-04-2025. This inspiring event was supported by the Punjab State Council for Science and Technology, highlighting a strong commitment to fostering innovation and scientific spirit among young minds. Students from DICE showcased an impressive array of innovative projects focused on Electric Vehicles, Internet of Things (IoT), sustainable energy solutions, and smart automation demonstrating the future-ready mindset and technical prowess of Chitkara’s budding engineers.

title: Indo-African Academia Industry Meet
content: Department of Interdisciplinary Courses in Engineering (DICE Chitkara University) presented their innovative project, “Smart Electric Wheelchair,” at the Indo-African Academia Industry Meet on hashtag#Healthcare hashtag#Innovations, held on April 7, 2025. The event was jointly organized by the Department of Healthcare Management, Chitkara Business School, and the DST-funded Chitkara University Technology Enabling Centre (CU-TEC). This project was mentored by Dr. Rajneesh Talwar, Professor and Dean, DICE. Foreign delegates from Africa attended the event and commended the innovation, calling it “a very good and impactful initiative that aligns well with current global healthcare needs.” The project bridges the gap between engineering and healthcare, embodying a true interdisciplinary approach to solving real-world problems.

title: Arduino/NodeMCU using Sensors
content: The Department of Interdisciplinary Courses in Engineering (DICE) at Chitkara University organized a hands-on workshop titled - “Arduino/NodeMCU Using Sensors” on April 4, 2025, at Turing Block (TG022). The session was led by Prof. (Dr.) Rajneesh Talwar, Dean, DICE, and Dr. Pardeep Kumar Jindal, DICE department. title: Innovative Ideas Implementation Using Drone
content: The Department of Interdisciplinary Courses in Engineering (DICE) at Chitkara University organized a workshop titled "Innovative Ideas Implementation Using Drone" on February 13, 2025. The session, focused on leveraging drone technology for innovation and real-world applications.

title: International Conference
content: Dr. Rajneesh Talwar's project paper on 'E-Bike' was selected at the International Conference, organized by DST-Centre, Panjab University, RFRF, FPTU-Vietnam, NTU-UK, and CICU.
